title: Complex numbers
examples: What is the definition of the imaginary unit i?
How do I use the conjugate when solving these equations?
Can you show me an example of solving a quadratic with complex roots?

explain.say: Today we begin with the imaginary unit i. By definition, i squared equals negative one. This means i is the square root of negative one.

items: i is the square root of negative one

explain.say: Next we look at arithmetic with complex numbers. If you add two complex numbers, you add the real parts and the imaginary parts separately. For example, (2 plus 3i) plus (1 plus 5i) equals 3 plus 8i.
The conjugate of a complex number is found by changing the sign of the imaginary part. The conjugate of three minus two i is three plus two i. We write this as 3 plus 2i.

items: Conjugate changes sign of imaginary part

explain.say: Finally we use these ideas to solve quadratics. When you solve an equation like z squared plus four z plus thirteen equals zero, you often find complex solutions. We use the quadratic formula to find them.

faq.q: What is the imaginary unit i exactly?
faq.a: The imaginary unit i is defined such that i squared equals negative one. It allows us to work with the square root of negative numbers.
asks: What is the value of i?

faq.q: How do I add complex numbers?
faq.a: You simply add the real parts together and then add the imaginary parts together separately. For example, two plus i plus three plus four i equals five plus five i.

faq.q: Why do I need to find the conjugate?
faq.a: Multiplying a complex number by its conjugate always results in a real number. This property is very useful when solving equations.
asks: What is the conjugate of 5 plus 2i?
How does the conjugate help me?

faq.q: Does the quadratic formula always work for complex numbers?
faq.a: Yes, the quadratic formula works for all quadratic equations, even when the solutions involve complex numbers. You just need to be careful with the negative signs.
asks: Can I use the quadratic formula here?
What if the roots are complex?

faq.q: What is the difference between real and complex numbers?
faq.a: Real numbers are numbers you are familiar with on a number line. Complex numbers have both a real part and an imaginary part, written as a plus or minus i times a number.
asks: Are all real numbers complex numbers?
What is the form of a complex number?

facts: The imaginary unit i is defined such that i squared equals negative one.
A complex number is written in the form a plus bi, where a and b are real numbers.
The conjugate of a complex number a plus bi is a minus bi.
When multiplying a complex number by its conjugate, the result is always a non-negative real number.

quiz.say: What is the value of i squared?
quiz.why: By definition, the imaginary unit i squared always equals negative one.

wrong.1: This is a common mistake because students sometimes forget the special definition of i.
wrong.2: This confuses the unit i with the result of i squared.
wrong.3: This incorrectly applies the sign change rule for the exponent.

quiz.say: What is the result of adding (5 plus 2i) and (1 plus 4i)?
quiz.why: You add the real parts five plus one equals six, and the imaginary parts two plus four equals six.

wrong.1: This incorrectly adds the real parts and then adds the imaginary parts separately.
wrong.2: This only adds the imaginary parts and forgets to add the real parts.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds only the real parts and forgets to add the imaginary parts.

quiz.say: If z equals 2 plus 3i, what is the value of z multiplied by its conjugate?
quiz.why: Multiplying by the conjugate always eliminates the imaginary unit i, leaving a real number.

wrong.0: While mathematically equivalent, this form is unnecessarily complex for the final answer.
wrong.1: This incorrectly subtracts the imaginary parts instead of multiplying.
wrong.3: This only adds the real parts and the imaginary parts, ignoring the multiplication.
